schema_adopted: A per-value CLAIM on each of the five guard thresholds dim_return_method states (tolerance, large_flow_share, plausibility_band_low, plausibility_band_high, comparability_max_excluded_weight), drawn from the law's four-member provenance set measured / inferred / held / absent (CLAUDE.md section 4; docs/doctrine/A_VALUE_MUST_CARRY_ITS_CLAIM.md). Declared domain of the claim: HOW THE ROW'S WRITER (emit_method_row) KNOWS THE THRESHOLD VALUE IT WRITES.
domain: how emit_method_row knows each threshold value it writes into a dim_return_method row

mece.finding: MECE over the declared domain, by subtraction from the printed denominator of FIVE threshold values: tolerance and large_flow_share are computed from the run's own data (measured); comparability_max_excluded_weight is computed from those two and the band by a stated formula (inferred); the two band ends are constants adopted without measurement (held); a value the code cannot produce is None (absent). Five values minus those four routes leaves ZERO values unplaced, and each of the four members has at least one producing line, so none is empty; a value carried in from a file with no stated claim is not a fifth way of knowing, it is a value the writer holds as given (held) and is marked as defaulted in a second field (see intent_coherence).

placed.absent: reachable for tolerance and large_flow_share (empty series -> None) and for the ceiling (UNDERIVABLE -> None)

same_grain.finding: The claim is PER THRESHOLD VALUE, the grain at which the ways of knowing differ inside one row: in the same row tolerance is measured while the band ends are held and the ceiling inferred, so a single row-level claim would assert one provenance over values that have three. The row itself stays at the table's grain (one row per method_version); five claims are properties of that row's five threshold columns, not new rows.

intent_coherence.finding: One axis, one intent. The claim columns answer ONE question, how the writer knows the value; they say nothing about whether the value is good, in tolerance, or applied. The second thing a consumer needs, whether the claim was STATED by the input or DEFAULTED by the writer because the input carried none, is a different axis and gets its own single field (threshold_claims_source = stated | defaulted_no_claims), so the member `held` is never overloaded to mean both 'deliberately held' and 'nobody told me'. The grading paths read the VALUES and never the claims, so the claim moves no verdict.

evidence.shows: the table answers one question: what arithmetic produced the numbers that point at it; the claim columns stay inside it
comparability() reads thresholds.get(...) the value, not a claim
guard_state_of reads thresholds[tolerance] the value, not a claim
emit_method_row today writes the bare number with no field a consumer can reject on

state_coherence.finding: Values one remedy does NOT move: re-measuring the guard moves tolerance and large_flow_share and, through the formula, the ceiling's VALUE, but not the band ends (held) and not the ceiling's CLAIM (still inferred); promoting a band end from held to measured moves that one claim and no value; filling a null value moves its claim off absent and nothing else; none of these moves a grading path, because the guard reads values, and none moves the already-served 49F row 2 partition, which is a different object written by an earlier run and is never rewritten by this change. The illegal states are refused: a claim outside the four, a null value under any claim but absent, and (the converse, same state) a non-null value claimed absent.

decision.field_family: threshold_claims = the thresholds-input key (an object, value name -> claim) and the name of the claim group; on the row it is written as one string column per value, tolerance_claim, large_flow_share_claim, plausibility_band_low_claim, plausibility_band_high_claim, comparability_max_excluded_weight_claim, plus ONE provenance-of-the-claim column threshold_claims_source (stated | defaulted_no_claims)
decision.where_written: BOTH surfaces, by one write: the six new columns are keys of the row dict in emit_method_row, so they land in the dim_return_method parquet (flat string columns, no nulls, readable by any engine without parsing a struct or JSON) and, because the manifest.json is {**row, thresholds}, in the manifest beside the thresholds echo that already carries the input's own threshold_claims object. The parquet column is the field a consumer rejects on. The returns tables are not written by this path.
decision.file_without_claims: A thresholds input that carries NO threshold_claims key is NOT refused and NEVER read as measured: emit_method_row writes, per value, claim `held` when the value is non-null and `absent` when it is null, and stamps threshold_claims_source = defaulted_no_claims. `held` is the one member that is true of a value the writer was handed with no statement of how it was got (the writer neither measured nor derived it). A threshold_claims object that is PRESENT but partial, with a key outside the five, a claim outside the four, a null value under a claim other than absent, or a non-null value under absent, is REFUSED. A thresholds input of None keeps its present behaviour (emit_method_row indexes it and fails; --method-row-only refuses it).
decision.reasoning: (1) Per-value grain, because the ways of knowing differ inside one row (same_grain). (2) Flat string columns, because the law wants a field a consumer can reject on, and a struct or JSON column is a field a consumer must parse. (3) Both surfaces in one write, because the manifest already spreads the row; no second writer. (4) The no-claims rule is `held`/`absent` + a source marker rather than a refusal, because a refusal would make every existing caller and test that passes a claim-less thresholds dict fail, and because the row-2 partition already served is never rewritten either way; and rather than writing `measured`, which would assert a provenance nobody stated, the exact defect the law names. (5) The source marker keeps `held` from carrying two meanings (intent_coherence), so a consumer can tell a deliberately held band from a defaulted claim. (6) comparability() and every grading path are untouched: they read values, never claims. KNOWN COST: the dim_return_method contract (org/standards, version 0.3.0) declares exactly the row's current columns and the round-10 check that equates them to the row dict literal will fail until the issuer bumps the contract (and that check pins version 0.3.0 itself, so the issuer re-pins or retires it with the bump); the contract is outside this order's grant and a surprise row is filed rather than hiding the columns from the literal to keep that check green.
